summary.title: Render text
summary.one_liner: You learn how to add player lives, a level-select menu with debounced key input, a win condition, and on-screen text feedback to a 2D Breakout game using a FreeType text renderer in OpenGL.
takeaways: Track player lives as a counter that decrements when the ball hits the bottom edge, and reset the level only when lives reach zero.
Use a KeysProcessed array so a key press registers once per press instead of repeating every frame while held.
Detect a win by checking that all non-solid bricks are destroyed, then switch to a GAME_WIN state.
Adjust glyph vertical position using the 'H' glyph's bearing when the projection has y going top to bottom.
summary.summary: The page is the final chapter of LearnOpenGL's Breakout 2D game series, extending the text rendering chapter. It adapts the TextRenderer to a top-down orthographic projection by offsetting glyphs using the bearing of 'H', then uses it for on-screen text. It walks through code for a three-life system, a level-select menu, key-press debouncing with a processed-keys array, and a win state that triggers when all non-solid bricks are destroyed. Code snippets are C++ with GLFW input handling.
